name: addons
description: UNVERIFIED FIRST DRAFT -- blind-authored from a plain-language description only, never run against real hardware. Login into the app, close any post-login notification dialogs, view the Add-ons screen, then log out. Steps 1-7 (dismiss system dialog through submit) are copied from the already-proven test-cases/login.json sequence (bugs 18-23, closed out end to end on real BrowserStack hardware for both platforms); steps 8+ (notifications, Add-ons, logout) are new guesses about this app's UI and have NOT been confirmed against a real screen. Expect this file to need the same bug-by-bug correction login.json did -- run it once via TESTOPS_MOBILE_BATCH_MODES=test-case, TESTOPS_MOBILE_TEST_CASE_FILE=test-cases/addons.json, and report back whatever the log/report actually shows so the guessed steps can be fixed from real evidence, not another guess.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
steps.note: REMOVED the speculative "tap Allow" step (and its dedicated CLOSE-recovery) that used to run before this one. Across 8 real runs, a pre-login Allow dialog never once actually appeared here -- every attempt at that step was either a correct no-op skip or, twice (addons-run-android-6.log: the ACTIVATE SIM container; addons-run-android-8.log: the home screen's "More Icon", opening an unrelated More-menu overlay), the resolver confidently guessing a totally unrelated element instead of declining, each time blocking this required LOGIN step from finding anything. A step with zero confirmed real use and two confirmed real harms is pure liability -- removed outright rather than patched again. A later plain-language CLOSE-dialog recovery step added for the ACTIVATE SIM case was REMOVED too (addons-run-android-10.log), by the same rule: zero confirmed correct firings across every run it ever ran in, and two confirmed harmful mis-fires onto the login form's own Back Arrow icon (addons-run-android-9.log, addons-run-android-10.log). The ACTIVATE SIM dialog's own real selector has never actually been captured in a page-source dump, so there is no evidence to hand-author an exact tapIfExists step for it yet -- only the LOGIN-retry step below covers that case for now, by simply re-attempting the real LOGIN tap. Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log (the Docker closing-verification run): the click's own next getPageSource dump shows the home screen's ACTIVATE SIM card gone and the login form's USE TAC tab present.

steps.instruction: close the More-menu overlay if it's open (More Close icon)
steps.note: REPLACED a plain-language, LLM-resolved "tap the small X-shaped close icon..." instruction with a hand-authored exact selector (kind: tapIfExists) after it mis-resolved onto the OPEN "More Icon" TWICE despite two separate rounds of rewording and resolver-prompt hardening -- addons-run-android-8.log (generic wording: "tap the More Close button to close the More menu popup", matched "More Icon"), addons-run-android-9.log fix attempt, then addons-run-android-10.log (explicit "only match when the overlay is already open" wording, STILL matched accessibility id "More Icon" and opened the overlay instead of closing it). A conditional "is this maybe-present thing here" step kept defeating prompt-level fixes because the resolver can be confidently wrong regardless of wording. `tapIfExists` removes the judgment call: the exact content-desc "More Close" (confirmed real, addons-run-android-10.log's page source) either exists (tapped) or doesn't (silently skipped) -- no LLM call, no guessing possible. See engine/semantic-act-executor.js's `exactSelector` option and docs/STATUS.md.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGIN button on the home screen to open the login form
steps.note: Retry of the LOGIN tap, only exercised when the first attempt mis-tapped ACTIVATE SIM instead, or the More-menu tapIfExists step above closed an overlay that had covered the login form -- optional so it's a no-op once the login form is already open. Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log: in that run this optional retry tap landed on the TAC/Password mode toggle (resolvedSelector resolves to a different element than step 0's, deeper inside the now-open form's ScrollView) and actually fired -- its own next page-source dump shows FORGOT PASSWORD appearing and the USE TAC tab disappearing as the form switches into password-entry layout.

steps.note: Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log: the login submit click's own immediate next page-source dump already shows the entire login form gone (Yes Number field label, Password field, FORGOT PASSWORD, the LOGIN button itself) with nothing yet appeared -- the real post-login content (the Allow-notifications system dialog, then the home dashboard) only renders a few polls later, during step 8's wait, so 'disappeared' is the only outcome this step's own diff reliably carries; appeared was left undeclared rather than guessed at a later step's evidence.

steps.instruction: wait for the login submission to finish and the notification-permission dialog to appear
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-5.log, a timing race rather than a wording/sequencing/resolver bug: login submission shows a progress spinner for a variable amount of time before the native 'Allow MyYes to send you notifications?' dialog actually appears. On addons-run-android-4.log the dialog was already up by the time the two 'tap Allow' steps below ran, so both resolved fine. On this run it wasn't -- both Allow taps correctly found nothing (optional, skipped as no-ops) while the spinner was still showing, and by the time the NEXT step (tap Add-ons) ran, the dialog had finally appeared and blocked it, failing the whole run with 'No elements match' since that step isn't optional. No step-sequence fix could have caught this: the dialog's arrival time varies run to run. Added this fixed pause (needed engine support: a new 'wait' step kind in engine/test-case-runner.js, since nothing could previously pause between steps) to give the dialog time to show up before either Allow-dismiss attempt runs.

steps.instruction: tap the Allow button to dismiss a system permission dialog if it's open
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-1.log: this app fires a native Android runtime-permission dialog ("Allow MyYes to send you notifications?", Allow/Don't allow buttons) right after login submit, not a custom in-app popup with a close/X button. addons-run-android-11.log's page-source finally captured this dialog's real resource-id (com.android.permissioncontroller:id/permission_allow_button, confirmed, with the sibling Don't-allow button at .../permission_deny_button) -- the plain-language version resolved correctly on that run, but converting now removes the same latent adjacent-sibling-button risk that caused bug #14 (CANCEL/SETTINGS) just one dialog later in this same file, before it has a chance to also regress here. Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log: tapping Allow's own next page-source dump shows the permission dialog gone and the first tutorial coach-mark tooltip (NEXT button + 'Your Account overview...' caption) appeared.

steps.instruction: close the coach mark tutorial popup if it's open (X icon)
steps.note: PROACTIVELY converted to tapIfExists (not from a new failure -- from re-auditing this file after the More-Close/CLOSE-dialog regressions, on the reasoning that any other plain-language 'maybe-present dialog' step in this file is the same latent risk, just not yet caught in a run). The exact resource-id (ivClose) was already confirmed on real hardware (addons-run-android-7.log's page-source, cited in this step's prior note) but had never been used -- this step was still being resolved by the LLM on every run despite the real selector being known. See docs/STATUS.md's "Thirteenth bug" for why a plain-language instruction is the wrong tool for a conditional step at all, independent of whether this exact one has misfired yet. Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log: in this run the tutorial carousel's NEXT steps never fired (no coach-mark was left to advance), so this ivClose tap's own settled page-source dump (the next one captured, since the following several steps were no-ops with no fresh diff) shows the tutorial tooltip's NEXT button gone and the real home dashboard (Hotspot, Profile, Account, etc.) rendered.

steps.instruction: advance the tutorial carousel if its NEXT button is showing
steps.note: PROACTIVELY converted to tapIfExists, same reasoning as the X-close step above -- the real resource-id (btnNext) was already confirmed on real hardware but unused. One tapIfExists step checked repeatedly covers the same 7-page carousel the old repeated plain-language NEXT steps did: each check is independent (found -> tap -> advance; not found -> skip), so repeating this step the same number of times has the same effect with zero chance of mis-resolving to something else on the screen.

steps.instruction: dismiss the 'Turn on Notifications' in-app popup via its CANCEL button if it's open
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-7.log (dialog identified) and addons-run-android-11.log (14th bug: the plain-language version of THIS step mis-fired). The in-app 'Turn on Notifications' dialog ('Notifications are turned off. Change your settings to allow notifications from MyYes app.') has two adjacent buttons: text="CANCEL" resource-id="android:id/button2" (left) and text="SETTINGS" resource-id="android:id/button1" (right) -- confirmed from addons-run-android-11.log's own page-source dump. The plain-language instruction, despite explicitly saying 'tap the CANCEL button, not SETTINGS, since the test should not navigate out to system Settings,' resolved onto button1 (SETTINGS) anyway, the exact outcome it was written to prevent. That single wrong click launched the device's system Settings app, and every subsequent step's resolver then made increasingly desperate guesses chasing 'Add-ons' through Settings and even Google Lens/search, ending up stranded on the home launcher screen -- a full cascade failure from one mis-click, the same resolver-overconfidence-on-adjacent-sibling-buttons bug class as the earlier CLOSE/More-Close regressions (bug #13). Converted to tapIfExists with the now-confirmed exact resource-id of the CANCEL button specifically, so no LLM judgment call between the two buttons is possible.

steps.instruction: tap the Add-ons tab or menu item
steps.note: CONFIRMED working on addons-run-android-2.log -- the guessed instruction resolved and clicked correctly; the run got past this step to the next (new) failure. CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-12.log/13.log (16th bug, user-reported with a screenshot): this app has no literal 'Add-ons tab' -- the resolver matches the dashboard's 'Buy Add-On' card (resource-id my.yes.yes4g:id/buyAddonLayout), a defensible call given the instruction's wording, which opens an Add-Ons purchase-details POPUP (Hotspot plan tiers, BUY NOW, Add-On Details/Validity) layered OVER the dashboard, not a navigable Add-ons screen. On addons-run-android-13.log this popup fully covered the bottom nav (unlike run 12, where it happened to leave Profile reachable underneath) -- the next tapIfExists Profile-tab step correctly found nothing and skipped (no mis-fire, working as designed), but with nothing left to close the popup, the required LOGOUT step's resolver then had no real button to find and confidently mis-clicked 'VIEW ALL' (my.yes.yes4g:id/tvViewAll) instead of failing -- a required step reporting false success on a wrong click, a new instance of the same resolver-overconfidence class, this time on a non-optional step. The run reported Succeeded: 1 despite never reaching Profile or Logout at all -- caught only because the user checked the actual screen, not from the report. Added a tapIfExists dismiss step directly below (confirmed selector my.yes.yes4g:id/ivClose, same resource-id as the coach-mark close button, reused by this app for its popup X icons generally) to close this popup before Profile is ever attempted.

steps.instruction: close the Add-Ons purchase-details popup if it's open (X icon)
steps.note: See the Add-ons-tap step's note above for the full real-bug evidence (addons-run-android-13.log). Without this step, the popup opened by tapping the dashboard's 'Buy Add-On' card blocks the Profile tab and leaves the required Logout step to confidently mis-click something else instead of failing cleanly. Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log: closing the Add-Ons purchase-details popup's own settled page-source dump shows the popup's BUY NOW button gone and the home dashboard's Buy Add-On card visible again underneath.

steps.instruction: tap the Profile or Account menu (bottom-nav tab) to find the logout option
steps.note: CONFIRMED working on addons-run-android-4.log with the plain-language version: the coach-mark/carousel fix got the run all the way past Add-ons into the Profile tab (bottom-nav item, resource-id ivProfile/tvProfile), landing on a menu screen (Billing Info, E-Bills, FAQs, General, Get Help, Settings, etc.). CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-12.log (15th bug): with a clearly labeled, unambiguous 'Profile' bottom-nav tab (text="Profile", resource-id="my.yes.yes4g:id/profileLayout") sitting right on screen, the plain-language resolver instead clicked "my.yes.yes4g:id/buyAddonLayout" -- an unrelated Buy-Addon card on the SAME Add-ons screen, with no textual or semantic relation to 'Profile', 'Account', or 'logout' at all. This opened an add-on purchase details popup (Hotspot 50GB/BUY NOW) instead of navigating anywhere near Profile, stranding the run there until the Logout step failed outright with no Logout button ever on screen. Not an adjacent-sibling-button mixup like bugs #13/#14 -- a flatly wrong match with a correct, clearly labeled candidate available. Converted to tapIfExists with the confirmed bottom-nav resource-id (stable across runs 4 and 12) so no LLM judgment call is possible here either. Evidence mined from addons-run-android-docker-5.log: tapping the Profile tab's own settled page-source dump shows the home dashboard's Buy Add-On card gone and the Profile menu (Settings, FAQs, Billing Info, etc.) rendered.

steps.instruction: scroll down on the Profile screen to reveal the Logout option
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug/gap on addons-run-android-4.log (original theory, since corrected -- see the LOGOUT step's note below): the Logout tap failed with 'No LOGOUT or Log Out button found' even though the Profile menu resolved correctly one step earlier. At the time, the working theory was that Logout sat below the fold in the Profile screen's scrollable menu, which motivated adding a 'scroll' action kind to the engine (engine/semantic-act-executor.js: a native mobile:scrollGesture/mobile:scroll gesture, no element resolution involved) and this step. addons-run-android-14.log's full page-source trace (scrolled all the way to the last menu item, 'About', with nothing below it) proved that theory wrong: Logout is never inside this scrollable list at all, at any scroll position -- see the LOGOUT step below for where it actually is. The 'scroll' engine capability and this step are kept as a harmless no-op (real gap, just not the one that was actually blocking Logout) in case a future build moves Logout back into the scrollable menu.

steps.instruction: tap the LOGOUT icon in the Profile screen's top header (next to the 'Profile' title) to sign out of the app
steps.note: CONFIRMED real bug on addons-run-android-4.log (wrong theory: thought Logout was below the fold in the scrollable menu -- see the scroll step above) and addons-run-android-14.log (17th bug, the real cause, found only because the user sent a screenshot of the actual Profile screen): Logout is not a text-labeled menu item at all. It's an icon in the Profile screen's top app bar, to the right of the 'Profile' title (an arrow-out-of-a-box glyph) -- confirmed from run 14's page source as a clickable ImageView with content-desc="Right Icon" (bounds [936,111][1062,237], top-right corner) and NO text anywhere in the accessibility tree relating it to 'logout' at all. A plain-language resolver can never reliably find this: there's no semantic signal to match 'LOGOUT or Log Out button' against a control labeled only 'Right Icon' by generic position, not purpose. Converted straight to tapIfExists on the user's own real-device confirmation rather than attempting another wording fix that, like the scroll theory before it, would have no real evidence behind it. CONFIRMED CORRECT on addons-run-android-15.log: tapping it opened a real native 'Are you sure you want to logout from the app?' confirmation dialog (Confirmation/YES/NO) -- proof this is the genuine Logout control, not another mis-fire.

steps.instruction: tap YES to confirm the logout confirmation dialog
steps.note: CONFIRMED real gap on addons-run-android-15.log: the LOGOUT icon step above correctly triggered a native confirmation dialog ('Are you sure you want to logout from the app?', NO=android:id/button2, YES=android:id/button1 -- confirmed from that run's own page source) that the test case had no step to dismiss. The run reported Succeeded: 1 even though the app was never actually logged out -- it was sitting on this unconfirmed dialog when the session ended, the same kind of report/reality gap flagged in bug #16's note (a 'succeeded' report is not proof of the intended real-world end state). Same adjacent-sibling-button risk as bug #14's CANCEL/SETTINGS dialog (button1/button2 reused generically across this app's dialogs), so tapIfExists with the exact confirmed id for YES specifically, never a resolver guess between the two.
